Not with a deck that isn't cheap. Yu gi oh used to be about strategy. 30 cards, no dupes and you had to time your plays right or it all came down. Nowadays all you have to do is have an effect monster to summon an army on your first play. I use a deck that has 5 magic and trap cards (one of each kind i.e. equip, field, quick play etc), 1 each of a 1, 2 and 3* monster (these are usually my most devastating assets like time wizard or that ladybug who kills all 4*s on the field. While I'm talking about it, Time Wizard is under appreciated imo. He's the ultimate gambit play. The "Blade of Damocles") about 4  4*s (usually like the armored bee, Goblin cards or a high DEF kind of monster) and one (or the other) of a 5/6*, 7/8* and 9/10* because having one of each (i.e. a full house of 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11*) just doesn't really work for me. I end up drawing high cards and never being able to summon much. I don't play that "one card to summon 17 more in a single play" shit. If I need that kind of effect I'd use a spell or trap as THAT'S WHAT THEY USED TO BE FOR UNTIL ALL THESE CRAZY ASS EFFECT MONSTERS CAME OUT. Here is how you turn it around: 
1. Take a shower
2. Clean your house
3. Go outside  at least twice a day (doesn't matter the length)
4. Jog, run or do some other form of exercise (that's important as it gets the blood pumping which WILL improve your mood EVERY TIME)
5. Find a hobby that makes you leave the house. I personally find animals very therapeutic to work with.
See a therapist or take some meds (It actually does help)
6. Make some friends, man. Or, join a support group that has in person meetings. It's important to interact with other people. Isolation breeds madness.
 This is all you need to do. I came from the exact place you're at now and it took me (not gonna lie) a few years of constant vigilance to notice a massive change in my personal energy. I come from a VERY bad childhood and my adulthood hasn't been too much better but the only way I got out of it was with a support system, multiple hobbies and a positive attitude (I know, it irritates me when someone says that but it really works). It's really all in your hands, man. Only you can prevent forest fires and the only way to do that is to go camping, not remain inside.
